QUESTION OF THE WEEK - The Reserve Bank Board meets Tuesday, and ahead of the meeting Reuters conducted its regular survey on the interest rate outlook. Full results are detailed seperately.
Briefly, of the 32 economists surveyed, 10 saw a rate cut in October as either likely or a definite possibility.
Of those surveyed, 23 see a cut as the next most likely move in rates, with November the most favoured month.
All of those expecting a cut saw it happening before year end.

RETAIL TRADE - Most expect some sort of correction to the strong 2.4 percent rise seen in July, but no one forecast a total correction. After a weak patch, economists said retail trade should probably start to show a slightly stronger trend in coming months, especially as the budget was well received by consumers and as the impact of the July 31 rate cut begins to flow through.

BUILDING APPROVALS - After the 8.1 percent rise in July, another rise, albeit a smaller one, is expected, reflecting signs that the trough may have passed in building approvals, although it would not be a sign that the industry is about to boom, economists said. A strong rise in July housing finance approvals should help building approvals, as should the two recent rounds of mortgage rate cuts.
